# dsh-plugin-mermaid-gb-svg

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns **Mermaid
flowcharts** into **GB/T 1526-1989** compliant **SVG*

* (the Chinese national standard, identical to
ISO 5807:1985), and exposes it to the model as one to

the Chinese national standard, identical to
ISO 5807:1985), and exposes it to the model as one tool.

> **Using it?** Star the repo — download
> counters are mostly mirrors and scanners, so a star is th
e one unambiguous "a person was here".

| GB/T 1526-1989 symbol chart | Generated flowchart |

## Compatibility
Tested against both current Harness lines — the engine suite (8) and the plugin suite (6) pass on ea
ted against both current Harness lines — the engine suite (8) and the plugin suite (6) pass on each:
| Harness line | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` / `dsh-sandbox` | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `@deepseek-ai/sc
ne | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` / `dsh-sandbox` | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` |

Every `@deepseek-ai/*` package is an **optional peer dependency**: the plugin uses the host's own
co

py, so no second runtime is installed inside the profile. The peer ranges list each Harness line
exp

licitly, because npm only admits a prerelease version when the range carries a comparator on that
ex
act `major.minor.patch` tuple — `^0.2.0-rc.2` does **not** match `0.2.1-rc.5`, and neither does `*`.

When the Harness opens a new line the range is extended; the matrix in
PUBLISHING.zh.md records wha
t has actually been run.
## Feedback
Feedback is what decides what gets built next — especially **standard-compliance corrections**, sinc

e
GB/T 1526-1989 has details that are easy to get subtly wrong.
| Channel | Use it for |
| Issues | Bugs, **symbol corrections** (there is a dedicated template — please cite the clause/figu

re), feature requests |
| Discussions | Usage questions, layout/typography opinions, open-ended idea

s |
| sandyyst@hotmail.com | Anything you would rather not post publicly |

**When reporting a problem, attach the Mermaid source.** A one-line description plus the `.mmd` is
u
sually enough to reproduce it — the generated diagram, the tool's `warnings` array, and your plugin

reproduce it — the generated diagram, the tool's `warnings` array, and your plugin
version help too.

If the tool reports geometry warnings, the output already carries the link to the issue tracker —
th
at is the moment the report is most useful.
